title: Mechanical clock
prompt: A labelled teaching model of the page 42 weight-driven pendulum clock has a suspended driving weight, gear train, minute and hour hands, escape wheel, anchor pallets and pendulum. Raise weight restores its stored gravitational energy as a teaching setup. Run lets the falling weight drive the train while the swinging pendulum alternately locks and releases the escape wheel and receives sustaining impulses. Slow view slows only the explanatory animation. The minute hand makes twelve revolutions for one hour-hand revolution, consistent with the 1998 wording and the pictured two gear reductions. See-through traces energy from weight to gears and escapement. Do not add an automatic watch rotor, balance hairspring, or mainspring to this chosen weight-driven variant.
blurb: A teaching adaptation of the page 42 weight-driven pendulum clock couples a falling weight, anchor escapement and twelve-to-one hand reduction.
adaptation: Schematic assembly of the clock gear lesson and weight-driven anchor diagram; added going-train ratios illustrate the connection, not a replica of a particular clock.
truthNotes: No mainspring, automatic rotor or balance hairspring.
Raise weight is an external teaching setup. Slow view only scales animation time.
Source motion-work pairs are 10:30 and 6:24. Added going train reduces escape speed 120:1 to the minute arbor.
Teeth and anchor contact profiles are schematic, not engineering profiles.
No production telemetry is installed. Live production verification is untested.
